label: Week 36, 2026
recap:
This week saw 15 bill movements across two jurisdictions, with California accounting for 13 of them and the United States Congress contributing 2. There were no case updates and no federal documents recorded, so the activity was concentrated almost entirely at the state level, largely driven by California's legislature.

Among the themes present, employment and hiring led with 4 bills touching on automated screening, workplace surveillance, and decisions about pay or promotion. Children and minors, health care, and privacy and data each had 2 bills, covering companion chatbots and age verification, clinical decision support and mental health chatbots, and biometrics and training data respectively. Infrastructure and energy appeared once, concerning data centers and their power draw. Seven bills did not fall under a specific theme. Overall, it was a modest week focused mainly on state-level legislative activity.

reading.body:
The week of August 31 to September 6, 2026 produced zero recorded activity in US AI policy or litigation: no bill movements, no court case updates, no federal filings.

A single week of silence in a legislative or regulatory record can reflect a recess, a filing deadline gap, or simply the limits of what the tracking system captures. The data does not distinguish between these possibilities, and no inference about a broader policy pause is warranted from one week alone.

What the data does not cover is as important to note as what it does. No bills, agencies, jurisdictions, or themes appear because none were logged, not necessarily because none existed. Readers drawing conclusions about the pace of AI governance should treat this week as a gap in the record rather than evidence of a trend.
